# Disable and re-enable the benchmark overlay from Customize

> Prove the performance chart removes the benchmark line and related legend when Benchmark is disabled and restores them when re-enabled.

## Step 1

Open {{start_url}} in a browser and wait for the ORBITAL dashboard to finish rendering with the Portfolio Performance card visible.

## Step 2

On the ORBITAL dashboard, confirm the performance chart currently shows the benchmark line and its related benchmark legend before changing Customize settings.

## Step 3

Open the Customize control and keep the right-side drawer visible while working with the chart options.

## Step 4

In the Customize drawer's Chart options section, clear the Benchmark option.

## Step 5

Assert on the Portfolio Performance chart that the benchmark line and its related legend element are no longer shown.

## Step 6

In the same Customize drawer, enable the Benchmark option again.

## Step 7

Assert on the Portfolio Performance chart that the benchmark line is visible again.

## Step 8 — assert @verifies ac-128, ac-138, ac-142

Confirm 'the benchmark line or its related legend element' does NOT appear (forbidden-presence) — the stated promise: Disabling Benchmark removes the benchmark line and its related legend element from the performance chart.

# Use keyboard navigation to toggle the Allocation section and verify reflow

> Prove the customize drawer controls remain operable with keyboard navigation and selection, with visible focus and no hover-only dependency.

## Step 1

Open {{start_url}} in a browser and wait for the ORBITAL dashboard to finish rendering with the Customize control visible.

## Step 2

Without using pointer interaction, move keyboard focus to the Customize control and activate it so the right-side drawer opens.

## Step 3

Use keyboard navigation inside the Customize drawer to focus the Allocation section toggle.

## Step 4

Assert that the currently focused Allocation toggle shows a visible focus indicator.

## Step 5

Store the current state of the focused Allocation section toggle as baseline_toggle_state and confirm it is checked before changing it.

## Step 6

Press Space on the focused Allocation section toggle to turn it off.

## Step 7

Assert that the Allocation section is not shown on the dashboard and that there is no empty dashboard slot where the disabled section had been.

## Step 8

Use keyboard navigation to focus the same Allocation section toggle again if needed, then press Space to turn it back on.

## Step 9

Assert that the Allocation section is visible on the dashboard again.

## Step 10

Confirm the Customize controls remained focusable and operable without requiring hover at any point in the test.

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Highest value because Benchmark toggle changes a core performance-chart reference line and its visible legend, so a broken effect would mislead a broad user-facing workflow.
[value_score] High value because Hover Indicators control a live chart affordance whose failure would make the toggle appear ineffective while leaving chart interaction inconsistent.
[value_score] High value because Grid visibility is a direct chart readability control and a likely regression point in rendering-layer customization.
[value_score] High value because keyboard-only operation and visible focus are cross-cutting accessibility promises that can silently fail even when pointer interactions work.
[value_score] Medium-high value because hiding a standard section and reflowing the adjacent layout exercises the core workspace-customization behavior on a typical dashboard card.
[value_score] Medium value because hiding a full-width section covers a distinct reflow shape, but it is less central than the chart controls and standard-card reflow.
[value_score] Medium value because default-option presence is important for orientation, but it is less failure-prone than live interface mutation and accessibility behavior.

[self_critique] Oracle fit checked: the test's written Check proves benchmark-removal absence directly against ac-138, while the re-enable step stayed narrower and asserted only the benchmark line because gap-22 leaves legend restoration unspecified.

[self_critique] Technique fit checked: hover-indicator and grid tests verify the specific visual effects named in the PRD and avoid over-broad claims about tooltip disappearance or broader chart redraw semantics that the source never promised.

[self_critique] Negative-coverage check completed: the corpus specifies successful toggle effects and reflow results but no invalid or rejected toggle states, so I did not invent negative tests; the section tests focus on proving absence of the hidden section and absence of the vacated slot.

[self_critique] Assert breadth checked: the defaults test limits itself to exact option sets and default enabled/selected states, and it does not claim any visible density-change effect because gap-21 leaves that oracle unresolved.
